subject: Designing what information reaches an LLM agent before it reasons — system prompt, persistent memory, always-loaded…

evals.prompt: Define context-engineering in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the context-engineering skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind context-engineering. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "improve this prompt's wording to get better outputs". Should context-engineering activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force context-engineering onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to prompt-craft, skill-router, context-window, tool-call-strategy, agent-engineering, skill-scaffold, code-review, epistemic-grounding.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "the agent ignored the instruction and used the wrong query helper — was the right skill loaded?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying context-engineering.

Place context-engineering among its adjacent skills (prompt-craft, skill-router, context-window, tool-call-strategy, agent-engineering, skill-scaffold, code-review, epistemic-grounding). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about context-engineering and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
